newsitem.title: BOSNIA: UN raps Croat charges against Moslems over violence.
newsitem.headline: UN raps Croat charges against Moslems over violence.

text.p: The United Nations said on Friday that Bosnian Croat authorities had no cause to press criminal charges against Moslems over ethnic violence with Croats in the divided city of Mostar.

Authorities in the west half of Mostar run by nationalist Croats have charged five Croat policemen with assault on a Moslem crowd on February 10, Croat media said on Thursday. One Moslem was shot dead and 21 wounded in the bloodshed.

But a Croat police statement said 11 Moslems, including two regional officials from the city's eastern sector, had also been charged with unspecified offences in the incident close to the city's internal ethnic boundary.

A U.N. inquiry found that Croat police opened fire without provocation on a group of Moslem pilgrims trying to visit a cemetery on the Croat side of the city and produced photographs to back up its finding.

"Our report made no mention of these (accused Moslems) and called for no action against them. We haven't seen the specific charges but judging by media reports they're totally irrelevant to the U.N. findings," said Liam McDowell of the U.N-affiliated International Police Task Force in postwar Bosnia.
A Croat police statement said that the charges were based on information from various sources including the IPTF report, videotapes, photographs and witnesses' statements.
It said five Croat policemen including deputy west Mostar chief Ivan Hrkac had been charged with "maltreatment while performing their duty". All were earlier suspended from duty.
But the list excluded former police chief Marko Radic, who was suspended for his role in the violence and later replaced.
The IPTF and other international agencies helping rebuild Bosnia from 43 months of war had demanded that all Croats involved in the shooting attack be prosecuted, including Radic.
